get.description: Signup mode for the sign-in screen, and the default timezone a new Schedule uses.

post.description:
Mail a Sign-in Code to an address — 202 whether or not it is anybody.

The answer must not vary with whether an account exists, or it becomes a
way to ask which addresses are on this instance. So there is nothing in
the body to differ, and the caller learns what happened by entering a code.
The issuance limit is the one refusal this route has, and it is about how
often the caller has asked rather than about who the address is.
Prove control of an address, which signs in — and signs up if it is new.

get.description: Who the caller is, and which Organizations they can act in.

delete.description:
End this account, behind typing its address — hard, and for good.

Every session goes with it, so the browser asking is signed out by the
answer it gets, and the cookie it still carries is taken back here. An
account that owns an Organization is refused: leaving must not leave a
team with nobody who can act for it.

patch.description: Change the display name. The email is the identity and is not editable.

post.description:
End this session — the row goes, and the browser stops carrying its key.

Other sessions of the same user are untouched; `logout-all` is the one
that reaches them.

End every session this account has, this one included.

The action for a browser the person no longer has — a phone left in a taxi,
a machine at an old job — so it deliberately reaches the sessions this
request cannot see, and takes the asking one with them.

get.description:
The offers this Organization has standing — never the spent ones.

An Invitation that was accepted, revoked, or has run out is not a thing
anyone can act on, so it is not on a list whose every row has actions.

post.description: Invite an address into this Organization, and mail it the offer.

delete.description: Withdraw an offer: the invitee stops seeing it and cannot take it up.

post.description:
Take up an offer made to this account's address, which joins the team.

Being signed in as the invited address is the whole of the proof, because
signing in is proof of the address the offer was made to.

Start a further Organization, owned by whoever asked for it.

Signing up makes the first one; this is every one after it — a second team,
a client's work kept apart from another's — and it answers with the same
shape the current-user view lists, because that is where it turns up next.

delete.description:
End the Organization, and everything that belonged to it.

The owner's alone, and behind typing the name: the Memberships, the
Invitations, and every piece of work the Organization owns go with it, and
nothing brings them back. Its people keep their accounts and their other
Organizations — what ends is the team, not the members.

patch.description:
Rename the Organization, which an owner and the admins may both do.

The name a signup made is the local part of an address, so the first thing
a team does with an Organization is give it their own name for it.

get.description:
Who else is here — a question every role in an Organization may ask.

Knowing who you work with is not managing them: the roles that gate this
screen's controls do not gate the screen.

patch.description: Move somebody between member and admin, which owners and admins both do.

delete.description:
End a Membership — an owner's or an admin's removal, or anyone's leaving.

Access ends with the row: the next request naming this Organization has no
Membership behind it, and the gate refuses it. The session is untouched,
because it is the account's and not this Organization's.

post.description: Hand the Organization to another of its members, and stay on as an admin.

get.description:
What this instance serves, and the oldest it will record with.

Unauthenticated: the app shows an out-of-date banner before a recording is
attempted, and the extension has no session of its own to ask with.

post.description:
Take a code to read out to the extension.

Authenticated, because the code is this person authorizing the pairing:
what spending it proves to the extension is that somebody signed into this
instance meant to connect.

Spend a connect code.

Unauthenticated: the extension has no session, which is the whole point of
the code. The commit happens before the refusal for the same reason the
Sign-in Code's does — a spent code must stay spent whatever the answer is.

Make an empty Workflow in the acting Organization.

Its Draft exists from this moment, empty: a recorder or an editor opening
a Workflow that has never been touched must find a document to write into
rather than a missing row.

get.description:
The acting Organization's Workflows, narrowed by what was typed.

Activity by default, because a list of automations is a list of what has
been happening; the other two orders are for finding one by hand.

One row more than was asked for is read, and dropped: whether a next page
exists is a fact about the data, and asking for it as a count would be a
second query over the same rows.

post.description:
Snapshot the Draft as the next Version.

The document is copied across as it is stored rather than re-serialized
through the models: what a Run reads weeks from now has to be what the
editor was looking at, down to the byte, and a round trip through code
that has changed since is exactly how that stops being true.

get.description: Every Version of this Workflow, oldest first, without their documents.
One published document, exactly as the publish that minted it left it.

post.description:
Copy a Version's document back into the Draft.

An edit of the Draft and nothing more: the Version stays where it is, and
what Schedules and Batches execute does not change until the user
publishes what they restored.

The document is not revalidated on the way in. It passed the rules at the
save that preceded its publish, and a Version is executable forever —
refusing to bring one back because a rule has since grown stricter would
make it exactly not that.

get.description:
What publishing would change, and where the Draft stands.

Against the latest Version and no other: it is what Schedules and Batches
execute, so it is the only thing "unpublished changes" can mean.
The Draft as one document: its Steps and the Variables they reference.

put.description:
Replace the Draft with the document sent, whole.

Whole rather than patched: the editor holds the document it is editing, so
a save is a statement of what the Draft now is, and there is no order of
arrival in which two saves leave a Draft nobody wrote.

post.description: Mint or rotate a one-hour token for this user and this Draft.
Keep only the newest full buffer; repeating a sequence changes nothing.
Replace the Draft from a recording, or patch one Re-pick target.

get.description:
One Workflow, as the same row the list would have drawn.

The Workflow page needs it: opened by its address rather than by a click,
it has no row to have carried the name and the draft state across. The
same query answers it, so the header a reload draws is the header the row
promised.

patch.description:
Change what a Workflow is called, and nothing else about it.

The name is the only field a row shows and the only one housekeeping
touches; the timeouts and the document have their own routes.

delete.description:
Delete a Workflow, and everything that only existed because of it.

Drafts, Versions, Schedules, Batches, Runs, Step Results, and Artifact
rows go with it on the foreign keys that already say so. Garage objects
do not: they are purged here, the same way deleting one Run purges them.
A live Run refuses the delete — two copies of one Workflow never act at
once, and deleting the Workflow under one would be the same as cancelling
it from the wrong end.

post.description:
A second Workflow holding a copy of this one's Draft.

The Draft and nothing else. Versions are not copied — a Version is what a
Schedule and a Batch execute, and a copy that arrived already published
would be an automation nobody has looked at that is ready to act on a real
website. The copy starts never-published, which is exactly true of it.
Persist one queued Run, then place its id on the dumb dispatch pipe.

get.description: Runs in newest-first order, optionally narrowed by Workflow and status.
The active Organization's non-terminal Run summary for the shell.
The persisted state a reconnect needs, in one payload.

delete.description: Purge a terminal Run, its rows, and its Garage objects.

post.description: Record where a new takeover domain should land on the next write-back.

get.description: Fan out `run:{id}:events` after the Organization gate; never replay.

200.description: Live Run events. Reconnection replays nothing.

get.description: The persisted log, optionally after a seq or for one Step.
Assembled on read from extract Step Results. Nothing is stored twice.
Mint a presigned GET after the Organization gate; never leak existence.

307.description: Redirect to a short-lived presigned URL

post.description: Cancel queued or waiting work now; stamp a request on a running Run.
Request takeover at the next safe boundary. Status stays running.
Mint a view-only ticket for any non-terminal Run.
Mint a control ticket for a waiting Run. One session holds it at a time.
Disable or re-enable auto hand-back for the rest of this takeover.
Ask the Worker to resume after a manual hand-back.
Give up during takeover: the Run fails and the browser can close.
The next five Occurrences of an expression. No Schedule has to exist.

get.description: Every Schedule in the active Organization, newest-created last.

post.description: Queue a Run of this Schedule now. Two copies never act at once.
Persist the rows and start the first queued one. Secrets never enter a row.

get.description: The Workflow's Batches, newest first, with counts derived from rows.
The Batch, its rows, derived counts, and an ETA once three rows finished.
One table: the union of the rows' Variables and extract output names.
Fan out `batch:{id}:events` after the Organization gate; never replay.

200.description: Live Batch events. Reconnection replays nothing.

post.description: Cancel the current Run and mark every remaining row cancelled.

patch.description: Edit a queued, skipped, or failed row's values. Status does not change.

post.description: Set one Variable on every queued row that has no value for it.
Cancel a waiting row's Run, mark it skipped, and advance at once.
Attach a new attempt to one finished row. Other rows stay as they are.

Account.title: Account
Account.description: Who the caller is. The email is theirs as they typed it.

AccountDeletion.title: AccountDeletion
AccountDeletion.description: The account's own address, typed by the person ending it.

AccountUpdate.title: AccountUpdate
AccountUpdate.description: The one thing about an account its owner may change here.

AssignableRole.title: AssignableRole
AssignableRole.description:
The two roles a Membership may be given.

Not owner: an Organization has exactly one, and it changes hands by the
transfer that replaces its holder — never by an offer somebody might never
take up, and never by a role change that would leave two.

CandidateKind.title: CandidateKind
CandidateKind.description: The ways of finding an element, in the order the recorder ranks them.

CodeRequest.title: CodeRequest
CodeRequest.description: Step one of the sign-in screen: the address to send a code to.

ConnectCode.title: ConnectCode
ConnectCode.description: A one-time code the app shows, for the extension's popup to take.

ConnectRequest.title: ConnectRequest
ConnectRequest.description: What the extension presents: the code, however it was pasted.

Connected.title: Connected
Connected.description:
Nothing — and deliberately.

The extension learns that the address it was given is a live instance that
accepted the pairing. Anything else here would be something an unauthenticated
caller could ask this endpoint for.

DraftComparison.title: DraftComparison
DraftComparison.description:
The Draft measured against the latest Version.

One answer for two readers: the publish modal renders the three lists, and
the Draft chip in the editor header — and the same chip in the Workflows
list — renders the state. They are one derivation because they are one
question, and two answers could disagree.

DraftState.title: DraftState
DraftState.description: Where a Draft stands against what has been published, in three words.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description: What every refusal this application raises looks like.

ExtensionVersion.title: ExtensionVersion
ExtensionVersion.description: The two versions an instance and its extension have to agree about.

ExtractField.title: ExtractField
ExtractField.description: One column of a list extraction, bound within the repeating element.

FrameHop.title: FrameHop
FrameHop.description: One step of the path into the frame an element lives in.

Instance.title: Instance
Instance.description: What an unauthenticated visitor may learn about this instance.

InvitationRequest.title: InvitationRequest
InvitationRequest.description: An offer to make: the address, and what it may do once it is taken.

LastRun.title: LastRun
LastRun.description: The newest Run of a Workflow, as the list row's meta line draws it.

ListExtractPayload.title: ListExtractPayload
ListExtractPayload.description: A flat list of records. There is no nesting, by decision.

Member.title: Member
Member.description: One person in an Organization, as its members screen shows them.

MintRequest.title: MintRequest
MintRequest.description: A new scope, or the id of an expired scope whose buffer must survive.

OfferedMembership.title: OfferedMembership
OfferedMembership.description: An Invitation as the person invited sees it: whose team, and as what.

OrganizationDeletion.title: OrganizationDeletion
OrganizationDeletion.description: The Organization's own name, typed by the owner who is ending it.

OrganizationMembership.title: OrganizationMembership
OrganizationMembership.description: One Organization a user acts in, and what they may do there.

OrganizationRequest.title: OrganizationRequest
OrganizationRequest.description: What an Organization is made and renamed with: a name people read.

OwnershipTransfer.title: OwnershipTransfer
OwnershipTransfer.description: Who the Organization is being handed to.

PendingInvitation.title: PendingInvitation
PendingInvitation.description: An offer an Organization has out, as its owner and admins see it.

RecordingMode.title: RecordingMode
RecordingMode.description: Whether a recording session replaces the Draft or repairs one Step.

Role.title: Role
Role.description:
What a Membership lets a user do in its Organization.

Exactly three, and an Organization has exactly one owner. Roles gate
membership and lifecycle actions only — every role does the domain work.

RoleChange.title: RoleChange
RoleChange.description: The one thing about a Membership that changes: what it lets them do.

ScalarExtractPayload.title: ScalarExtractPayload
ScalarExtractPayload.description: One named value: an element's text, or one of its attributes.

SelectorCandidate.title: SelectorCandidate
SelectorCandidate.description: One way of finding an element, verified unique when it was recorded.

SignedIn.title: SignedIn
SignedIn.description:
What signing in tells the screen: whether this visit made the account.

The screen needs it to decide between welcoming someone and letting them
carry on, and it is the only thing that differs between the two.

StepRef.title: StepRef
StepRef.description: One Step in a diff: what names it in a modal, and nothing else.

TakeoverPayload.title: TakeoverPayload
TakeoverPayload.description: What the person is asked to do, and how the Run can tell they did it.

Target.title: Target
Target.description: How a Step finds its element: candidates best-first, and where they live.

Unsupported.title: Unsupported
Unsupported.description:
A target the recorder captured and expects replay to fail on.

The warning is written at capture, in plain language, because the person
who can still do something about it is the person recording.

UnsupportedReason.title: UnsupportedReason
UnsupportedReason.description: Why a recorded target will not be findable again, whatever we do.

Variable.title: Variable
Variable.description:
A named input a Workflow declares. Step values reference it by name.

A secret Variable may point at a vault Secret by id. The name beside the
id is a cache for display: renaming the Secret never rewrites a Version,
and a deleted Secret still has a name to show.

VerificationRequest.title: VerificationRequest
VerificationRequest.description: Step two of the sign-in screen: the address, and the code it received.

VersionSummary.title: VersionSummary
VersionSummary.description: A Version without its document — what a version dropdown lists.

WorkflowCreation.title: WorkflowCreation
WorkflowCreation.description: Everything creating a Workflow asks for: what to call it.

WorkflowDocument.title: WorkflowDocument
WorkflowDocument.description: A Draft, or a Version, as one value: the Steps and the Variables.

WorkflowNamed.title: WorkflowNamed
WorkflowNamed.description: A Workflow and what it is called: what renaming and duplicating answer.

WorkflowPage.title: WorkflowPage
WorkflowPage.description:
One page of the list, and where the next one starts.

`next_cursor` is absent on the last page, which is how a caller knows it
has reached the end: an empty page would be one request too many, and a
count would be a second query nobody asked for.

WorkflowRecord.title: WorkflowRecord
WorkflowRecord.description:
The Workflow row itself, without its document.

What creating one answers with. The list has a summary of its own, richer
and joined against the Draft and the Versions; this is the plain row.

WorkflowRename.title: WorkflowRename
WorkflowRename.description: Everything renaming asks for. A name is all a row shows of a Workflow.

WorkflowSort.title: WorkflowSort
WorkflowSort.description:
The three orders the list offers, and nothing else.

Three rather than a free-form order-by: every one of them is a keyset the
cursor can be built on, and a fourth would have to earn its index first.

WorkflowSummary.title: WorkflowSummary
WorkflowSummary.description: A Workflow as a list row: everything the row draws, and no document.
